card.name: Giving two products together or in sequence
card.fires_on: The verb 'administered', 'administer' or 'taken' right after 'be' or 'or', where the text says whether two drugs or products may be given together, one after the other, or apart.

modes.label: Allowed sequentially
modes.description: 'may be administered' followed by sequential or simultaneous use of ceftriaxone with calcium products.
modes.example: ceftriaxone and CLINIMIX E may be<< administered>> sequentially if the infusion lines are thoroughly flushed

modes.label: Do not give together
modes.description: 'administer' in a warning not to give two products simultaneously via one line.
modes.example: Do not mix Calcium Chloride Injection with ceftriaxone or<< administer>> these products simultaneously via a Y-site because

modes.label: Oral spacing
modes.description: 'taken' before 'at the same time' or 'within' a time window for supplements or binding agents.
modes.example: supplements or multivitamins containing calcium or iron can be<< taken>> at the same time.

card.writes: It promotes words about closeness (proximity, nearby, vicinity), suggesting the next words describe how near in time or place two doses are.
card.plain: It marks the verb 'given' or 'taken' when the label is about whether two products can be given at the same time or close together.
